answer: Per-key sealed storage ties each seat to its own slow-sealed replica. Every identity stores about 50 GB of uniquely sealed data keyed to its private material, then answers random spot checks that probe a ridge of seal hashes, a plume of challenge offsets, and an onyx-tagged sector digest within 5 seconds. One shared disk image fails because sealing is slow and key-specific; 200 fakes need about 10 TB of distinct sealed stores that cannot be pooled onto one drive.
